propositions: When a ticket description exceeds the configured cap (verify.max_ticket_description_chars, default 8000) and the plan-review claim gate is enabled, a warning must be emitted at save time (create or edit) across all surfaces (CLI stderr, library logger, MCP result field), stating the actual length, the cap, and that claim review will refuse admission until the description is shortened.

The save-time warning must reuse the same config key and gate enablement probe (_plan_review_gate_applies) as the plan-review admission guard to ensure consistent behavior, avoiding promises the gate would not keep.
The warning must never block or alter the ticket write; it is computed after the CREATE/EDIT event is appended and degrades to None on error, so the save always succeeds.
No warning is emitted when the description is within the cap, when the plan-review gate is disabled, or when the ticket type is exempt from the gate.

The warning must be surfaced through three channels: CLI prints 'Warning: …' to stderr (keeping stdout pure in text and json modes), library logs it on the rebar logger (edit_ticket returns str|None, create_ticket(return_alias=True) carries description_warning in the dict), and MCP includes an optional description_warning field in CreateResultOut and WriteAckOut.

Config key verify.max_ticket_description_chars is pre-existing and shared by the review guard (det_floor P4) and the completion precheck; this change adds a third reader rather than introducing a new key, preserving single-sourcing.
